chunks: As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was their treasure. And their father was righteous. So your Lord willed that they reach their maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord. That is the interpretation of that over which you could not bear with patience.
ai.seo_question: What is the deeper meaning behind Khidr repairing the wall of the two orphans?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the concept of *al-Bari'* (the Divine Maker) who acts according to His hidden wisdom (*hikmah*) rather than human perception, linking the orphans' future maturity to the preservation of their father's righteousness (*salatuhu*). It underscores that Khidr’s seemingly erratic actions were actually precise divine interventions to secure the orphans' inheritance, serving as a mercy (*rahmah*) that transcends immediate human understanding. This narrative is often cited to illustrate the distinction between *zahir* (apparent) and *batin* (hidden) realities in divine decree.
